slides.title: What is a Hyperlink? 🌐
slides.content: # The Threads That Weave the Web Hyperlinks (or just **links**) are the foundation of the World Wide Web. They let users jump from one page to another, download files, send emails, or even make phone calls. In HTML, a link is created with the **anchor** element: ``. ```html Start Learning ``` The `href` attribute holds the destination URL. The text between the tags is what users click.

slides.title: Linking Beyond Web Pages 📧📞
slides.content: # Email and Phone Links - **Email:** Use `mailto:` followed by the email address. Optionally add `?subject=`. ```html Email Us ``` - **Phone:** Use `tel:` for phone numbers (works on mobile devices). ```html Call Us ``` These protocols trigger the default email client or dialer.

quizData.question: The `href` value can only start with `http://` or `https://`.
quizData.explanation: It can also begin with `mailto:`, `tel:`, or even just a fragment (`#section`).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Make Link Text Meaningful

Avoid 'click here'. Instead, use descriptive text like 'Download the report' or 'View our pricing'. It helps screen reader users who navigate by links.
